question.worked_solution:
Let $u={x}^{3}$, Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{x}^{2}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u={x}^{2}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡({x}^{3})\operatorname{tan}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =\int \operatorname{sec}⁡({x}^{3})\operatorname{tan}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \operatorname{sec}⁡u\operatorname{tan}⁡u\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int \operatorname{sec}⁡u\operatorname{tan}⁡u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sec}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sec}⁡({x}^{3})+C\end{aligned}
$$
